title: Trump faces ‘bipartisan pushback’ on diesel deal with Russia as he tries to lower prices
summary: News panel on the Russia diesel deal: the Iran war, not Ukraine, is driving fuel prices, and a few million barrels of Russian diesel cannot materially lower them.

assertions.quote: IT'S THE WAR IN IRAN THAT'S LARGELY CAUSING FUEL PRICES TO RISE.
TO MAKE PROBLEMS FOR OUR FARMERS, OUR RANCHERS WITH DIESEL FUEL, BECAUSE RUSSIA SUPPLIES A LARGE PORTION OF THE DIESEL FUEL THROUGHOUT THE WORLD.

verdicts.note: Russia was the second-largest diesel exporter and its export ban after refinery strikes tightened global supply, but the Iran war and Gulf disruption are the larger factor.

assertions.quote: 2.25 MILLION BARRELS OF DIESEL THAT THIS DEAL COULD PRODUCE IS LESS THAN A DAY'S SUPPLY FOR THE AMERICAN TRANSPORT SECTOR.

verdicts.note: US distillate consumption is around four million barrels a day, so a one-off shipment of a few million barrels is a rounding error in a global market.

assertions.quote: THERE'S VERY LITTLE THAT THEY CAN ACTUALLY DO TO MATERIALLY BRING DOWN THE COST OF DIESEL SHORT OF END THE IRAN WAR

verdicts.note: Export bans and reserve releases give only brief relief in a globally priced fuel market; the supply disruption itself sets the price.
